title: BNCI 2016-002 Emergency Braking during Simulated Driving dataset
description: EEG, EMG and vehicle-dynamics recordings from 15 healthy participants who drove a simulated racing car while following a lead vehicle that occasionally braked abruptly, requiring emergency braking. The dataset supports research on detecting a driver's braking intention from brain activity before the behavioral response, using event-related potentials and machine learning for driver assistance and neuroergonomics. It is a preprocessed BIDS conversion distributed through the BNCI Horizon archive.
methods_description: Participants drove a virtual car (TORCS) with a steering wheel and gas/brake pedals at 100 km/h, following a computer-controlled lead vehicle that decelerated abruptly at 20-40 s intervals. Three 45-minute blocks were recorded with a BrainAmp amplifier (59 EEG channels, plus EMG and EOG, nose reference). Signals were lowpass filtered at 45 Hz, synchronized and resampled to 200 Hz.
